title: Planning and Logistics Lead
leads: The hub attendants and the runners. One attendant per hub per night, and one runner for every three hub sites in the same area.
where: The store at the Central Cairo warehouse, the two hubs, and the sites on the schedule
hours: Days at the store, six days a week. Reachable until the last run is in at 10:00 PM
summary: You plan where every phone and person goes, and you run the store, the hubs, and the runners that get them there.

posting.headline: Planning and Logistics Lead (planning, store, hubs, and runners), Cairo
posting.about: We run video recording teams at factories, warehouses, farms, and construction sites across Cairo. Workers wear a small camera on a cap while they do their normal job. The Planning and Logistics Lead plans every move: which phones and people go to which site, and when. You run the store, the two upload hubs, the runners, and the buying in Egypt, so no site starts short and no phone sleeps full.
do: Write the dispatch schedule and the site plan for every new site: phones, people, and the date.
Keep the sheet that maps each industry to a job type and an app category.
Turn the schedule into procurement demand: what to buy, how many, and by when.
Buy gear in Egypt: phones, mounts, caps, chargers, and cables. Keep spares at ten percent.
Run the store at the Central Cairo warehouse. Keep the phone registry. Build every kit.
Run the two hubs, Central and East, and their internet lines.
Run the runners and the hub attendants: the nightly plan, the spare list, and the morning return.
Run the weekly count on Thursday: registry, MDM, and room say the same number.
need: You have run a store, a warehouse, or a team of drivers before.
Careful with a list. Every phone has a row, and every bag has a signature.
Good with a schedule. You see next week's shortage today.
Calm on the phone at 9:00 PM when a runner is late.
plus: You have bought equipment in Egypt and dealt with suppliers.
You have planned people and equipment across more than one site.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
Your own store, two hubs, and a team of runners and attendants.
Every procedure written down: the schedule, the kit, the hub night, and the run.
A daily line to the Director of Operations.
posting.apply: Send your name, where you live, a phone number, and the stores, fleets, or teams you have run. We call back within two working days.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of Planning and Logistics Lead at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the Director of Operations.
Your start date is {start}. In your first weeks you take over the store, the registry, and the hubs, and you write your first dispatch schedule with {manager}.

handbook.purpose: The client pays for accepted hours. Those hours need a phone on a head at the right site, a hub that empties it overnight, and a runner who brings it back by 7:00 AM. You plan every move, and you run every piece that moves. A site that starts short, a hub with a dead line, or a run that is late is yours to fix the same day.
outcomes: Every new site launches on the day the schedule named, with a whole kit.
Every run is at a hub before 10:00 PM. Every phone is back at its site before 7:00 AM.
The registry, the MDM, and the room say the same number every Thursday.
The spare pool never falls under ten percent.
daily: Morning. Read the hub numbers sent before 7:00 AM: phones in, out, and held. A held phone is a call to its Portfolio Manager.
Morning. Check the dashboard for phones still holding footage. Change tonight's plan if a site needs a run.
Same day. A short store or a dead hub line. Order, or open the ticket, now.
By 4:00 PM. Tonight's plan to every runner and attendant: which sites, which hub, which bag.
Before 6:00 PM. A runner missing at the end of the shift is replaced from the spare list. Call the spare now.
10:00 PM. Every run on the plan is in, or Moharam knows which is not.
Meet Moharam with the schedule, the stock, and what is short.
weekly: Thursday, 4:00 PM. The weekly count at the store, every site, and every hub: registry, MDM, and room match.
Once a week. Next week's launches against the stock. Short means order today, or the date waits.
Once a week. Check the spare list. One spare runner per hub area, ready to be called.
monthly: Month end. Turn next month's site plans into procurement demand. Send the buying list to Ahmed Alaa for approval.
Month end. Go through the month's runs and hub logs with the runners and attendants. Agree on what to change.
standards: The schedule names every phone and person from today's stock, never from another site's kit.
No site launches short. If the plan says short, the date waits.
One attendant per hub per night. A second when a hub takes more than 150 phones a night.
One runner for every three hub sites in the same area, with a vehicle. One spare per hub area.
The morning return is the same runner and the same three sites as the night before, all phones back before 7:00 AM.
Sites on the west side and 6th of October upload on site or run to Central until a West hub is live.
Nobody signs for a count that is not their count.
Money to Ahmed Alaa, quality to Youssef Medhat, papers to Mano. Nobody contacts the client.
never: A kit filled from another site's kit.
A run that cannot reach the hub by 10:00 PM does not leave.
A phone that goes home, or an account that is shared, ends the job.
Saying the client's name to anyone outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: In the store with Moharam. The registry, the kit list, the tags, the hubs, and the runner plan.
Run the Thursday count and one full hub night yourself. Write tonight's runner plan every day.
Write one dispatch schedule and site plan end to end. Build the kit. Moharam checks every phone before the handover.
One launch on the day you named, with a whole kit. Moharam signs you off.

measures: Launches on the day the schedule named, with a whole kit.
Runs at a hub before 10:00 PM, and phones back before 7:00 AM, every night.
The Thursday count: every difference explained the same day.
Days the spare pool was under ten percent.
handbook.call: Moharam, for the schedule, a late run, or anything you cannot settle. Ahmed Alaa for money and the buying list. Youssef Medhat for a flag. Mano for papers. An injury or the police: Moharam, then Adham.
